![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14199831/assets/e7c6cb8f0d7746c1d923ed80a9e05ba4f8eeb9ea3ae88c7b08bcd02037d8ec8a.png)

The two triangles shown above are similar. What is the correct similarity statement?
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the measures of unknown angles. Since the sum of the measures of internal angles of a triangle is ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠H+m∠J+m∠L & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠H+{69}^{∘}+{40}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠H+{109}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠H & ={71}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠V+m∠W+m∠Y & ={180}^{∘} \\ {71}^{∘}+m∠W+{40}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠W+{111}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠W & ={69}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the triangles are similar, and

$$
\begin{aligned}∠H≅∠V,\,∠J≅∠W,\,∠L≅∠Y.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that 

- $H$ corresponds to $V,$

- $J$ corresponds to $W,$

- $L$ corresponds to $Y.$

Therefore, $HJL∼VWY.$
